challenge.name: The Override Blind Spot
challenge.description: Store managers are overriding order suggestions at an alarming rate because they cannot verify if the model behind them is the one they tested. #model_monica# wants a fully automated registry to ensure every deployment is traceable and reproducible. #requirements_reuben# has a red line: no model enters the registry without a manual, documented review of its evaluation metrics to ensure compliance, so he insists on keeping the process manual.

output.content: We need to close the gap between drift detection and the training pipeline. Right now, when a feature drifts, the alert sits in a dashboard while the next retraining cycle proceeds on stale assumptions. I want the hand over to be fully automated so the system reacts in hours, not days. Every additional layer of manual review in that specific path just delays the correction. The goal is to catch the shift before it hits the morning order window, so the forecast stays reliable for the store managers who are already skeptical. More automation here directly reduces the risk of a silent failure, and I am happy to push for more aggressive thresholds if that is what it takes to keep the signal clean.
output.reclassify_reason: The author explicitly states that more automation directly reduces risk and expresses a willingness to push for more aggressive thresholds, indicating that exceeding the basic request for automation would make them happier.
